name: clawmetry-setup-openclaw
description: Pinned OpenClaw CLI for the setup-openclaw composite action. CI-only: nothing here ships in the clawmetry wheel or is imported by the dashboard.
//overrides: The openclaw pin is 2026.9.2. At the pins recorded below `npm audit` reports
2 moderate advisories and 0 high and 0 critical. The two that remain are
named and explained at the end -- they are not an oversight and neither has
a fix this tree can take.
WHAT THIS CORRECTS (2026-11-13). The previous revision of this note said 'the
tree is advisory-clean, npm audit reports 0 vulnerabilities', and by
2026-11-13 that had quietly stopped being true. Nothing in this directory had
changed. New advisories had simply been published against the exact versions
these overrides pin, and an exact-version override freezes the tree against
exactly that drift. Measured on this branch:
before  12 advisories / 5 high / 0 critical
after    2 advisories / 0 high / 0 critical
The five highs were @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, body-parser, undici, zod, and
openclaw's own roll-up of those. Every one had a fix inside the major this
tree already resolves, so the fix was to move the pins, not the openclaw
version. Each pin below was re-measured rather than bumped to 'latest'.
THE FIRST LESSON. An exact-version override is a dated measurement, not a
standing guarantee. It does not drift forward when a patch lands and it does
not warn you. So treat a clean `npm audit` quoted in this file as evidence
about the day it was run, and re-run it rather than reading this note and
believing it. That is how five highs sat here unnoticed.
EACH PIN, re-measured 2026-11-13 at openclaw 2026.9.2:
tar@7                        7.5.23    load-bearing, hoisted root
undici@8                     8.12.4    clears GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c (high)
ws@8                         8.23.0    load-bearing

body-parser@2                2.4.0     clears GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 (high)

The three inert keys stay for the reason they always have: each is a no-op
while its package is absent and each becomes correct again the moment a
future openclaw pulls that package back in. Delete them only with a fresh
audit in hand.
Keys stay range-scoped (name@major) for the original reason: a bare `undici`
key would also rewrite any undici@7 a transitive resolves, which is a major
bump for that consumer. `basic-ftp` is the one bare key, and the reason it is
safe is recorded with its 2026-10-01 measurement in git history. It is inert
now anyway.
THE SECOND LESSON, learned the hard way on this very change: VERIFY WITH
`npm ci`, NOT `npm install`. A cross-major override key was tried here --
`minimatch@10` resolving to 11.0.8 -- to clear the two moderates below. It
took the tree to 0 advisories and `npm install` accepted it without a
murmur. `npm ci`, which is what this action actually runs, then refused the
lockfile it had just written:
npm error `npm ci` can only install packages when your package.json and
npm error package-lock.json [...] are in sync.
npm error Missing: minimatch@10.2.6 from lock file
So the key was dropped. The cost of not catching that would have been every
caller of this action failing at install, which is the whole E2E fleet. A
clean `npm install` plus a clean `npm audit` is not evidence that this
directory works; `npm ci` from a deleted node_modules is.
RUN THE BOOT GATE TOO, FOR ANY CHANGE TO THIS FILE OR THE LOCKFILE. This is
the older lesson and it still holds. `npm ci` succeeds and `openclaw
--version` prints a version even when the module graph is broken: neither
loads the graph. The gate that catches it is booting the gateway, which is
what .github/workflows/openclaw-boot.yml does:
openclaw gateway --port 18789 --verbose --allow-unconfigured
# then poll http://127.0.0.1:18789/ for any HTTP response
It reproduces locally in about five seconds and logs 'http server listening'
then 'ready' when the tree is sound. Run it, not just --version.
Boot gate run for THIS change, on Node 22.23.4: HTTP 200 after ~6s, 'http
server listening (13 plugins: anthropic, browser, canvas, cua-computer,
device-pair, file-transfer, geolocation, linux-node, memory-core, ollama,
openai, talk-voice, xai)', 'ready', 'heartbeat started', on OpenClaw 2026.9.2
(3928bad) -- the same 13 plugins and the same commit the previous revision of
this note recorded, so none of the moved pins disturbs the module graph.
`npm ci` from a deleted node_modules was run twice and installed 332
packages both times.
THE TWO MODERATES THAT REMAIN, and why neither is taken:
minimatch  GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249, globparts amplification, range >=7.0.0
<11.0.1. The tree holds 10.2.6, so there is no fix inside 10.x
and no in-major pin can clear it. The cross-major key that
would is the one `npm ci` rejected above. npm's own offered
alternative is openclaw 2026.4.29, a five-month downgrade.
openclaw   The roll-up of the minimatch finding above, not a separate
defect. It clears when that one does.
WHY THE OPENCLAW PIN DOES NOT MOVE HERE. `npm audit` offers openclaw 2026.11.3
as the fix for four of the five highs and for the minimatch moderate. That is
a real option and it is deliberately not taken, because the newer releases
raise engines.node past this action's bare `22` default and moving that moves
every caller -- ci.yml (live-openclaw-e2e), e2e-nightly.yml,
moat-keystone-drive-nightly.yml, openclaw-boot.yml, oss-golden-path.yml and
pr-screenshots.yml, all six of which take the default. A Node major for the
E2E fleet is a decision with an owner; clearing published highs in CI tooling
is not. The pins above clear every high without touching Node, so that
decision stays open rather than being forced by an advisory. Taking it is
what would also clear the two moderates.
THE MIRROR IN clawmetry-cloud. vivekchand/clawmetry-cloud carries a copy of
this action pinning the same openclaw 2026.9.2 with NO overrides block, and
it refreshed its lockfile on 2026-11-13. Measured the same day, that copy
reports 5 advisories / 4 high -- the same mcp-sdk, undici, zod and openclaw
roll-up this block now clears. The two copies share a mechanism rather than a
release cadence, so this is reported there rather than cross-pushed; the fix
there is an overrides block like this one, not another lockfile refresh,
because a refresh is what it already did.
